cards.explanation: The answer is touch, friends. The people beg Jesus to touch the blind man (Mark 8:22). Not a speech, not a ceremony, just a touch. I think they knew exactly what they were asking for.

The answer is out of the village, friends. Jesus takes the blind man by the hand and leads him out of the village (Mark 8:23). Think about that walk. The man can't see where he's going, and he holds on anyway. I think that's a whole lot of trust in one handhold.

The answer is False, friends. The man says, “I can see the people, but they look like trees walking around.” (Mark 8:24) He can see, but not clearly yet. I think that's a wild thing to say out loud, and honestly, I respect his honesty.

The answer is that Jesus places His hands on the man's eyes again, friends (Mark 8:25). The man told Jesus what he saw, and Jesus went right back to work. Nobody gets hurried out the door here. I like that a lot.

The answer is True, friends. When the man opens his eyes this time, his sight is restored, and he can see everything clearly (Mark 8:25). From trees walking around to clear as day. That's a big change in one moment.

The answer is “Do not go back into the village,” bakers. Jesus sends the man home and says those very words (Mark 8:26). The text doesn't say why, so I won't guess a reason. I'll just say it's a good one to remember word for word.
